transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, they brought me in because of what happened at the fair. I was supposed to be giving a talk, you know, about equipment and patterns in the field—folks don’t always understand how the rows talk to each other, especially with the newer tractors—and I climbed up onto the tractor right there.

I started jerking the controls around to show everybody the “new pattern,” and people were yelling at me to stop, but I just… I couldn’t make myself stop. It got out of hand, I guess.
During this, have you heard voices or seen things that other people could not?

Yeah… I mean, not like seeing a person standing there exactly, but I hear them. Out by the north pasture mostly, when it’s getting toward dusk and the light goes all flat across the rows. It comes through the irrigation lines—clear as anybody talking—telling me which rows are poisoned and which ones are blessed.

And folks think it’s just pipe noise, but I know the difference. I’ve listened to water lines my whole life. It’s not only when I’m worked up, either… it still happens on weeks when I’m not all fired up.
Do you hear those voices only when you’re feeling especially energized or worked up?

No, not only then. I mean, there were weeks—quieter weeks—where I wasn’t especially wound up or thinking I was meant for something big or anything like that. I’d just be doing regular chores, checking numbers, feed, water, rows… and the lines would still talk.

And the farm data too, the printouts and readings, they’d still feel like they had warnings tucked inside them. Hidden ones. It’s hard to explain because most people just see numbers, but when you’ve worked land as long as I have, you know when something’s trying to tell you something.
Before the voices and hidden messages started, had you begun using any drugs or had any major medical illness or head injury?

I don’t know… I mean, I don’t think so? I’ve been around chemicals and fuel and machines my whole life, so it’s hard to say what counts as “using” something or getting hit hard enough to matter.

I had my share of bumps—every farmer does. You crack your head on a beam or slip off something and you just get back to work if the cows still need feeding. But nothing that I remember where a doctor said, “This is the cause,” or anything like that.

As for drugs, no… not like that. I was always more worried about keeping equipment running. You miss one maintenance window and then the whole week gets eaten up by repairs, and then the weather turns, and then everybody acts surprised like the land doesn’t keep its own schedule.
Before the fair happened, was there a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… before then, I wasn’t sleeping right at all. Most nights I’d maybe get two, three hours in the chair, boots still on sometimes, or I’d just not sleep. Then I’d be up before the sun like I’d been plugged into something, ready to work the whole place like nothing had happened.

And you know, on a farm there’s always something that needs doing, so people don’t think much of it. A man gets up early, that’s just what he does. But it was more than that. I didn’t feel tired the way I should’ve.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices or noticing hidden messages, but you were not feeling especially energized, high, or unusually up at the same time?

Yes… yes, there were stretches like that. More than one, I think. Quieter weeks, you know—not me running around like I had some big purpose or feeling all charged up.

I’d just be doing normal work, checking the rows, feed, water, numbers on the sheets… and the lines would still talk. The farm data still had warnings in it, like there were messages tucked under the regular figures. People think numbers are just numbers, but out there you learn to pay attention.

So, yes—there were several weeks where I wasn’t especially up or grand, but it was still happening.
Have there been times when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it that exactly. I’ve had low spells, sure. Everybody does when the season goes bad or a calf’s sick or the bills stack up and the tractor decides to quit at the worst possible time.

But “most of the day nearly every day for two weeks”… I’m not real good at marking it out like that. Days kind of run together on a place like mine. You get up, you do what has to be done, whether you feel one way or another.

So I guess I’m not sure. Maybe sometimes I was down, but I couldn’t tell you cleanly if it was like what you’re asking.
Have you ever had a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

I’m not sure I can say that cleanly. I’ve had days where I felt heavy, like everything took more effort than it ought to, but nearly all day, almost every day… I don’t know.

On the farm you don’t always get to sit and measure how you feel. If the fence is down, it’s down. If something needs fed, it needs fed. You just keep moving, and sometimes later you realize you weren’t right for a while. But I couldn’t tell you for sure if it was like what you mean.
From when the voices and hidden messages first began, did they continue for at least one month?

Yes… definitely more than a month. It’s been, I’d say, around eleven months now since the voices and those coded warnings started showing up.

At first I thought maybe it was just a bad stretch, like when equipment keeps breaking and you start seeing patterns in everything because you’re tired. But it didn’t just pass after a week or two. It kept going—through chores, through paperwork, even when things on the place were otherwise normal. So yes, much longer than one month.
When the voices first started, were you feeling completely normal in your mood at that time?

Not completely, no… or, I mean, it wasn’t like I was all fired up or feeling larger than life the whole time either.

There were quieter weeks in there where my mood felt more level, I guess. I wasn’t especially energized or grand or anything like that. Just doing the usual—checking numbers, feed, weather reports, all that—except I could still hear those lines talking, and I still believed the farm data had warnings tucked inside it.

It’s hard to explain, because on a farm there’s always something talking at you in a way—machines, wind, the cattle making noise—but this wasn’t just that. Even when I wasn’t in some big mood, it was still there.
During those energized times, did you feel unusually powerful or important?

Yes… during those times I did feel like that. Like I was the one farmer in the county who could see it plain, this whole new way of growing things, and everyone else was too slow or too stuck in their habits to understand.

I kept thinking the university people, the lenders, all of them, they ought to be listening to me instead of doubting me. Because I’ve worked land long enough to know when something’s possible, you know? They sit in offices and talk numbers, but they don’t feel the soil in their hands or watch a field change after rain. So yes, I did feel… unusually sure I was important in that way.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when you felt unusually energized or high nearly every day?

Yes… there have been stretches like that. I’d wake up some mornings and it felt like the whole valley was opening up just for me, like everything was lined up right, and I’d be grinning at nothing before the coffee was even done.

But then—well, it could turn quick. If a hired hand questioned what I was doing, or my wife told me I needed to slow down, I’d snap like they’d insulted the family name. And that’s not like arguing over a busted gate or a late delivery, you know, that happens. This felt bigger in me. Nearly every day for a while, yes.
Have there been at least two weeks when you were hearing the voices or seeing hidden messages while your mood felt neither unusually high nor depressed?

Yes… there were. More than two weeks, I’d say.

There were several quieter weeks where I wasn’t all charged up or thinking I was some big important man with the answer to everything. I wasn’t especially energized or grand. I was just… doing chores, looking over numbers, feed, weather, the usual farm data.

But the voices were still there. The lines still sounded like they were talking, and I still believed there were warnings hidden in the farm data. It wasn’t just when my mood was high. It kept going even when I felt more level.
